==International statistics and estimates==
According to statistics from the European Union, the actual population has been reduced by at least 230,000 people who emigrated into European Union member states between 1998 and 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.balkaninsight.com/en/article/report-macedonia-drained-by-migration|title=Macedonia Population Drained by Emigration, Report Says |website=[[Balkan Insight]] |date=15 May 2013 |access-date=2017-08-29}}</ref> Further Albanian news sources estimated at October 2012 that the real population is closer to the sum of 1,744,237 people who are accounted within all of the health funds of the country.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.balkaneu.com/fall-number-population-fyrom/|title=Fall in the number of population in FYROM|website=Balkaneu.com|access-date=2017-08-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.echedoros-a.gr/2013/10/blog-post_3784.html|title=Σκόπια: Σημαντική μείωση του πληθυσμού|website=Echedoros-a.gr|access-date=2017-08-29}}</ref> According to [[Bozhidar Dimitrov]], the Bulgarian authorities have granted 87,000 to many of those emigrants a [[Bulgarian passport]], as of 2012, which requires that they declare to be ethnic [[Bulgarians]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.plusinfo.mk/vest/75328/Bozhidar-Dimitrov-86000-Makedonci-izvadile-bugarski-pasosh|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130111011838/http://www.plusinfo.mk/vest/75328/Bozhidar-Dimitrov-86000-Makedonci-izvadile-bugarski-pasosh|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 January 2013|title=Божидар Димитров: 86.000 Македонци извадиле бугарски пасош|date=11 January 2013|access-date=15 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://a1on.mk/wordpress/archives/82774|title=Димитров: 86.000 Македонци досега извадиле бугарски пасош|date=8 January 2013|website=A1on.mk|access-date=2017-08-29|archive-date=2016-03-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304073922/http://a1on.mk/wordpress/archives/82774|url-status=dead}}</ref> Since Bulgaria's entry into the European Union, and under pressure from fellow European Union members, Bulgaria imposed more stringent rules and measures for the acquisition of a [[Bulgarian citizenship]] and passport.

The provisions of the [[Ohrid Agreement|Ohrid agreement]] to elevate any minority language if the minority in question is above 20% of the population of any municipality into a co-official language for that municipality has created friction within the government, and between officials of different political and ethnic interests, resulting in the indefinite postponement of the census for almost twenty years until it was finally conducted in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Trkanjec|first=Zeljko|date=2021-10-04|title=North Macedonia 2021 census is over|url=https://www.euractiv.com/section/politics/short_news/north-macedonia-2021-census-is-over/|access-date=2021-10-23|website=www.euractiv.com|language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Ethnic groups==
The process of industrialization and urbanization after the Second World War that caused the population growth to decrease involved the [[Macedonians (ethnic group)|ethnic Macedonians]] to a greater extent than Muslims. Rates of increase were very high among rural Muslims: [[Turks in North Macedonia|Turks]] and [[Macedonian Muslims|Torbesh]] (Macedonian Muslims) had rates 2.5 times those of the Macedonian majority, while [[Romani people in North Macedonia|Roma]] had rates 3 times as high. In 1994, Macedonians had a TFR of 2.07, while the TFR of others were: Albanian (2.10), Turkish (3.55), Roma (4.01), Serb (2.07), Vlachs (1.88) and Others (3.05). The TFR by religions was: Christian (2.17, with 2.20 for Catholics and 2.06 for Orthodox), Islam (4.02) and others (2.16).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.newbalkanpolitics.org.mk/OldSite/Issue_2/dragovic.eng.asp |title=New Balkan Politics - Issue 2 |access-date=2010-05-15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928043220/http://www.newbalkanpolitics.org.mk/OldSite/Issue_2/dragovic.eng.asp |archive-date=2007-09-28 }}</ref>

However, it is unlikely that this high minority TFR has continued since then in North Macedonia, as Balkan fertility elsewhere ([[Demographics of Albania|Albania]], [[Demographics of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Demographics of Kosovo|Kosovo]]) has dropped sharply toward the European average. A more recent survey<ref>{{cite web |url=http://blogs.channel4.com/factcheck/factcheck-will-britain-have-a-muslim-majority-by-2050/13690 |title=FactCheck: Will Britain have a Muslim majority by 2050? &#124; the FactCheck Blog |access-date=2013-06-14 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130617231159/http://blogs.channel4.com/factcheck/factcheck-will-britain-have-a-muslim-majority-by-2050/13690 |archive-date=2013-06-17 }}</ref> pegs Muslim fertility in North Macedonia at 1.7, versus 1.5 for non-Muslims.

In 2017, 21,754 children were born in North Macedonia. The ethnic affiliation of these newborns was: 11,260 (51.76%) [[Macedonians (ethnic group)|Macedonian]]; 7,404 (34.03%) [[Albanians in North Macedonia|Albanian]]; 940 (4.32%) [[Turks in North Macedonia|Turkish]]; 1,276 (5.87%) [[Romani people in North Macedonia|Roma]]; 40 (0.18%) [[Aromanians in North Macedonia|Vlach]]; 129 (0.59%) [[Serbs of North Macedonia|Serbian]]; 213 (0.98%) [[Bosniaks in North Macedonia|Bosniaks]]; 492 (2,26%) other ethnic affiliation and unknown.<ref name="Statistical Yearbook of the Republic of Macedonia, 2018">''{{cite web |url=http://www.stat.gov.mk/Publikacii/SG2018/03-Naselenie-Population.pdf |title=Statistical Yearbook of the Republic of Macedonia, 2018, p. 83 |publisher=North Macedonia, State Statistical Office |date=2016|access-date=20 October 2018}}''</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stat.gov.mk/PrikaziPoslednaPublikacija.aspx?id=41|title=Државен завод за статистика - публикација: Основни и средни училишта на крајот на учебната година|website=www.stat.gov.mk|language=mk|access-date=2018-11-24}}</ref> In the school year 2016/2017 there were 192 715 students in elementary schools from which 104,756 (55%) were [[Macedonians (ethnic group)|Macedonian]], and 60,971 (32%) were [[Albanians|Albanian]], and in High schools there were 72 482 students from which 43,658 (60.1%) were [[Macedonians (ethnic group)|Macedonian]] and 22 419 (30.9%) were [[Albanians]]. Furthermore, in 1999 [[Albanians]] accounted for 34.6% of newborns and 26.1% of students who finished high school in 2016, which was regulated by the Ministry of Education.

== ''CIA World Factbook'' demographic statistics ==
The following demographic statistics are from the ''[[CIA World Factbook]]'', unless otherwise indicated.

===Age structure===
* 0–14 years: 19.5% (male 210,078; female 203,106)
* 15–64 years: 67.8% (male 707,298; female 696,830)
* 65 years and over: 12.7% (male 97,437; female 124,661) (2004 est)

===Sex ratio===
* at birth: 1.08 male(s)/female
* under 15 years: 1.08 male(s)/female
* 15–64 years: 1.02 male(s)/female
* 65 years and over: 0.78 male(s)/female
* total population: 1 male(s)/female (2004 est.)

===Infant mortality rate===
* total: 11.74 deaths/1,000 live births
* female: 10.73 deaths/1,000 live births (2004 est.)
* male: 12.67 deaths/1,000 live births

===Life expectancy at birth===
* total population: 74.73 years
* male: 72.45 years
* female: 77.2 years (2004 est.)

===Total fertility rate===
* 1.50 children born/woman (2015 est.)<ref name="europa.eu">{{cite web|url=http://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/tgm/table.do?tab=table&init=1&language=en&pcode=tsdde220&plugin=0|title=Eurostat - Tables, Graphs and Maps Interface (TGM) table|website=ec.europa.eu|access-date=15 December 2017}}</ref>

===HIV/AIDS===
* adult prevalence rate: less than 0.1% (2001 est.)
* people living with HIV/AIDS: less than 100 (1999 est.)
* deaths: less than 100 (2001 est.)

===Nationality===
* noun: Macedonian/citizen of the Republic of North Macedonia<ref name=prespa>Under the terms of the [[Prespa agreement]], the nationality of the country will be called "Macedonian/citizen of the Republic of North Macedonia" in full.</ref>
* adjective: Macedonian / of North Macedonia<ref name=prespa/>
